holding_summary: A city ordinance authorizing the Mayor to order occupants of a house of prostitution or assignation to remove, with fine or imprisonment for refusal, is a valid exercise of delegated police power and does not deprive the owner-keeper of due process, even though she owns the premises.

quotes.text: The charter of the city expressly delegates the power to “ regulate houses of prostitution and assignation ” and “exclude such houses from certain limits” and “to close the same,” and “to authorize the Mayor to close such places.”

It is the clearest possibleuexample of a police regulation, the exercise of the police power of the State — that power reserved to every State, as essential to social order and comfort, which subjects the most absolute rights of properly to the condition that they shall be so used as not to infringe the rights of others.

notes: Borderline relevant: deals with municipal police-power closure of a house of assignation (owner-occupied, used for short-stay occupancy) rather than an ordinary boarding/lodging house; court does not characterize the arrangement under lease/license/lodging/innkeeping terms, so characterization left null; duration of individual occupancies not stated.

holding_summary: A lodging housekeeper who retains a room in her house to be occasionally visited and occupied by her concubine, without any contract for payment of rent, cannot recover room rent or nursing fees, because the arrangement was merely incidental to the pre-existing concubinage rather than a genuine letting for pay.

quotes.text: 1. A woman who keeps a room in he? house to bo visited and occasionally occupied by lior concubine, without any contract for the payment of rent by the latter, cannot enforce such payment.
the plaintiff, a lodging housekeeper in this city, claims $1644 90 for room rent due by Joseph Mathis

But are we to hold that that woman or man who keeps a room in his or her house to be visited occasionally and occupied by a concubine, without any contract to pay rent, can claim or enforce such payment?

Nevertheless he continued to make regular weekly visits to the house of plaintiff, spending there Saturday night, Sunday and Sunday night. It was on these occasions that he occupied the room for which rent is claimed, and which was undoubtedly, retained for his occupancy and not rented to others.

notes: Court's reasoning implies an ordinary lodging-rent contract would have been enforceable (favorable-leaning dicta), but denies recovery on these facts because the occupancy was incidental to concubinage rather than a bona fide letting for pay; marked mixed.
